title: John Abraham reflects on Atlanta Falcons Ring of Honor Induction Ceremony | Press Conference
text: Yes, go ahead with the questions. So, hey Abe, how are you feeling tonight before we go onto the field at halftime? Wow, more nervous than I was when I was playing.  When I played, it was like you were wearing a helmet, so nobody could see you.  So, if you ruin Arthur Blank's name, you might never step onto the field again.    That's why I try to stay very calm and enjoy the moment.  We have about a minute and a half to talk, and since I've been doing this, you know, podcasts and all that, I've gotten used to long sentences, so I had to compress everything to include everyone I need to mention. And what will that speech be like? What's the title? What will the main story be? The speech, probably, Tamika Rush told me, was one minute and 30 seconds long.  So , you know, you don't have as much time as you'd like, but you want to stick to the basics, more or less.  You know, I want to thank the people who were here when I was here.  I want to thank the people who are here now, who are my family.  And trying to think about...Well, I can thank you all now, the reporters and everyone, because I know you...I haven't had any bad reviews in a while.  I think they've been doing a good job keeping my name out of the mud. I think I've put that behind me now, and I thank everyone for that.  Everyone who has written about me, whether on or off the field, always had something good to say.  And my mom, my dad, my children are here, and I can say that they always tried to keep my name as clean as they could.  Are you going to practice it, or is it something that, when the time comes, you'll simply want to let flow? We did the rehearsal yesterday, and I got to see all the things that were going to happen. But it will still be different, because when the crowd screams, my emotions ... because you know, I have my family here, and I know I'm not a softie, but when you get to a certain age, it's like the tear ducts or something. It's like something hits him and triggers him, making him cry over anything, especially since they 're all girls, so I'm more sensitive than anyone.  I grew up in a house full of women, and then I had only daughters, so it's all just about trying to be protective. So, when I see certain things, I automatically lose control and I ... but, but I'm going to keep my glasses on, friends, just in case the tears come.  They're not going to put me on live television like that. John, I've been through Timmonsville before, and I immediately think of you.  What does it mean to you to represent your hometown through the way you play ?  I mean, it's not a very big city, but you being a guy from South Carolina and always representing your home, what does that mean? Uh, it means a lot.  Like I said, my mom is here.  Um, coming from Timmonsville and uh someone asked me a question last night.  They asked me, "Does this seem unreal to you?"  I said, "Of course. "  I said, "But, but uh on my way back to be and try to become a better person, I had to go back to my illusions of being in Timmonsville, going to school in Lamar."  I had to do it, I had to go back to those times when I imagined being here.  So, this is where I should be, and this is where I'm supposed to be.  Um, I'm trying to do the best I can now that I'm done and get back to being the honorable person I used to be.  So, the Ring of Honor means a lot to me just because of that last word, honor .  You know, I want to be seen that way, and the other 14 guys that are there, and the other guy that will be included uh later this uh year, look at those guys, man.  They are very well-known figures.  So, even my 55 being right there with them and alone, you know, just the fact that your name is there with Arthur Blank, Matt Ryan, you know , Warrick Dunn.  If you...no, I couldn't imagine this.  Even now, I still ca n't imagine it, man.  So, I'm trying to live in the moment and uh try to absorb it all.  Good. You were an active player, did you look up and think that one day it could be you? When I was an active player in 2012, I thought I was going to make it to a Super Bowl.  So I had a broader vision , and now this is my overview.  Realistically, in 2012 I thought we had a Super Bowl caliber team.  I thought we were going to get there.  You couldn't tell me we didn't have the best team in the league and, you know, it was a shame I couldn't play.  And it's as if my entire career has been like this with injuries.  They always arrived at the wrong time.  So, did I imagine it?  Not at all.  Like, not at all.  When I received the call, I knew that my friend Terrell Clary had a lot to do with it.  I know she's very persistent when it comes to me.  So I know she chimed in and said, "Hey, hey, look at my brother ."  "Look at my brother."  So I know she had a lot to do with it.  That definitely helps, and just respect, man.  Only respect.  You listen to Matt.  You listen to Arthur Blank.  These guys, just like Rich McKay.  There are so many people in this organization. Even you, Larry.  You know, you were always coming to bother me by asking, "Will you speak today?"  Do you know what I mean?  You know I talk on Wednesdays , my friend.  I know.  Alright.  But it's good to see you, man. Hey, but looking back on the whole career.  135 captures.  30.5 or 33.5. 48 forced loose balls.  How proud are you of your career, and what do you say to people about what Ron Medlin did to make sure you got rid of those core injuries that led to those 40? Well, you hit the nail on the head.  Hey, let me ask you something.  That's why I don't like you , Matt, because I haven't talked to you about that.  But that was one of the people I was going to thank.  I was going to thank him because, you know, he's in Baltimore now.  And literally, if you look at my career, if you look at when I was with the Jets, injury after injury after injury.  I got injured the first year here and then I didn't have any serious injuries for the rest of my career.  So Ron took matters into his own hands.  Maybe because of the 45 million they gave me.  Don't know. But he said, Ron put it in his hands and said, "Look, we're going to find someone because we're tired of you having the same injury."  And then, we went, we went to Canada.  He took me to Canada and found a guy named Nico Berg.  And we started working.  And also, the Falcons actually said we need you on Sunday.  So all this stuff about Wednesdays, hitting yourself and doing all this, is because you train like you play.  So it's a little different.  You don't really rest on the plays like that. So we had to make you rest during the plays and it worked. But Ron Medlin was, is Ron Medlin, Rod Walters, like David Price, all these guys dealing with injuries and dealing with so many things.  You, you dealing with injuries, dealing with family, dealing with football;  It's like the whole core is something you feel should be the worst part of your problems if you've never been injured before.  So yeah, Ron, Ron is my friend, man.  Ron, there are so many, John. It's like, there are so many guys I could mention right now.  But I was definitely going to mention Ron Medlin. Who called you? What was it...?    It wasn't a call.  It was, it wasn't a call.  Actually, um Jackson, they , they prepared me very well, because you know, I've been trying to be an active father.  I've been trying to do everything, like my daughter needs to do this, my daughter wants to do this, I try to show up here.  So he contacted me about 2 months before.  He said, "Look, let's do some flag football for girls."  And you know I'm talking about 2 months and you know me, hey, just let me see the questions first.  Okay , let me have the questions.  I don't want to look stupid when I'm on television.  So give me the questions.  He, I mean, said he gave me the questions.  I asked her what to wear.  He said, "Oh, come casual, you know."  So they got me good, man.  And the first person who really told me that it was for me was my daughter Ayumi.  Happy birthday, Ayumi .  He turned 18.  Everyone should be very proud of her for that. Okay? Anything else? Thanks, guys.  Enjoy your day, man.

title: HC Kevin Stefanski & QB Michael Penix Jr. Post-game Press Conference | Week 5 | Falcons vs. Ravens
text: Okay, injury front. Uh CJ Henderson has a groin injury. Mike Pennix has a rib injury. We'll know more on both of those uh as we get imaging and those type of things. Uh you know, that's credit to Baltimore. That's a good football team. Uh obviously, we didn't do enough to win that game. Uh we had really missed opportunities and and when you're playing a good football team and these margins are razor thin like we knew they would be, uh we got to we got to uh come through on some of those plays. But, uh that that's all of us as coaches, that's players. we can be better in those moments and then you can put a good football team away uh late which uh we did not do and then again give them credit. They came back and scored and and u did a nice job. So uh we'll learn from it. Um disappointing, frustrating, all those things but we will learn from it. I'll take any questions you got. >> No, no, nothing specific. Uh I mean yeah there's plays that we we can make. There's calls that we can give our guys to be better. Those type of things, but uh in a game like that, there's all these little plays add up to being the big play. >> At what point did you know Mike was not going to be able to go back in? It looked like there was some debate. Was it on the fence or was it >> Yeah, he was trying to work to get comfortable and and could not. >> This game early became less of a bejon or less of a run game and more on Mike than we had seen the last two weeks. Was that game script? Was that something the Ravens defense was doing? Yeah. Uh, all the above. I I think again that's where I give credit to their defense. Uh, you know, they had their adjustments, we had our adjustments. Um, but ultimately we just we have to uh have to find a way to get in the end zone a few times more. >> Your defense had been so good against the run, got gashed a little bit tonight. Does that just come with the way that y'all play up front that can happen or did you feel like you didn't execute? I think run defense, again, give credit to Baltimore, but run defense is about, you know, doing our job, getting off blocks, tackling, and uh we just didn't do that well enough tonight, but there's things that we can certainly can do better from player perspective and a coach perspective. >> Kevin, in in overtime, were you concerned at all about the the time that was on the clock with how the defense was managing that? >> Yeah, I mean, that's part of these rules when it's, you know, 10 minutes that a long drive by that on that first drive can bleed, you know, your opportunities. Now, we got the ball with plenty of time in our minds to go try to go score, but uh obviously we didn't come through. >> Um when you look at what you were able to do uh in the fourth quarter on third down, converted at two third and 10 or third and 15, does that give you like some positive momentum like when the tape? >> Yeah, third and long is hard in this league as you guys know. Uh and I thought, you know, we had some opportunities there uh to to make plays and we did. Uh, but I go back to what got us in those situations and and trying you really want to stay manageable versus a good football team and and we have to do a better job of that. >> You all were able to kind of flip the script time of possession wise first half to the second half. Was was that intentional to give your defense some some rest and what kind of went into that? I I think time of possession and and it just is a matter of playing good offense and when you play good offense, you possess the ball and and we hit hit on some things in the second half uh which were positive, but bottom line is uh we got to come through uh when it matters. >> Uh the last two games the team had been pretty effective in the red zone, uh especially running the football in those areas. What was different about what happened tonight? I don't know what the statistic was what we came out, but again, there's there's plays that, you know, you give them credit, they they knocked us back a few times in the run game and then uh we just didn't score enough points and and it's it's the collective we we didn't do a good enough job. Coaches, players, offense, defense, special teams, we we'll own this one together. >> Pre-injjury, how did Mike play in your eyes tonight? I thought, you know, listen, versus a tough defense of front, a tough coverage, I thought made some plays, like every quarterback, you're not going to make every play, but there's things that he can certainly improve upon, but um I thought he battled. >> You guys haven't quite played in one like that where you led late. To have it slip away, how surprised are you about that? And when you watch it back, what do you think you'll see about kind of why it slipped, how it >> Well, it's the NFL. you're going up against good football teams and when you have opportunities to put them away and and score a touchdown or or whatever it might be and make that one extra play, that's what you have to do versus these guys. And that's just us as a team. You know, we we will own this one together and and we'll find ways to be better in those moments. >> Mike was obviously emotional on the sideline and I know you still have imaging to do, but what are some things that you as the coaching staff can do to rally around him potentially during this time? >> Yeah, I don't Tori, I don't know if I know enough yet um to to be fair. So, uh, we'll support all of our guys like we always do and and we'll see as, uh, we get more information. >> Anything else? >> Okay. Thank you. >> How's it going? Start. >> Mike, can you kind of take us through the last like couple minutes of the game? What happened? How were you feeling? and and what were you trying to work out on the sideline? >> Yeah. Um first of all, I just want to thank God, you know, um it's a tough sport. It's a tough sport, physical sport, you know. Um you know, I I got hit pretty good and, you know, just trying to trying to u get back out there. You I did I did take some throws on the sideline just to see how I felt. And I did not feel like I was going to be able to, you know, give our team uh what we needed to to be able to help us win that football game because of, you know, the pain that I was feeling. Um, so, um, that's that's all that happened. You know, I was trying to get out there. I feel like if we had the, uh, if we had the ball first and in overtime, I probably would have been out there, but as you know, we were sitting, you know, um, you know, what I was going through, it just started getting worse and worse as we were just sitting there. I was getting cold. >> I know it's difficult, but when you're sitting there and you're obviously emotional, can you take us into kind of what you're feeling kind of knowing that you're not going to be able to go out there? Yeah, it's emotional because, you know, um you know, it's tough, you know, I always want to be out there. I want to uh be able to I want to be able to finish every game, you know, um and obviously I got a history of not not doing that, you know, but um you know, I just going to continue to trust in God, you know, what I'm going through right now. I know it's not something that's going to be a longterm thing, you know, but uh today um it it took it took me out for the last couple minutes of the game, you know, but um I'll be all right. know knowing you know knowing your body the way you do you said not a long-term thing but and I know you haven't seen any imaging or anything but any idea you know what what that might be >> I don't know see me knowing me I I'm be I'm be ready to go next week cuz I ain't I sat I sat out enough in my career but u I'm going to do everything I can uh in the training room you know make sure I get back to where I want to be um you know but obviously you know uh my health is very very serious I take that very serious so you know that's always going to come first, but I will work my tail off to make sure I'm back out there on that field. >> Have you dealt with rib issues in the past? >> I did. Yeah, actually um in college, you know, but uh that was a long time ago, but um we all good though. >> Is this anything similar to that or different? >> I don't know. I ain't get imaging yet, so we'll see. >> Fair enough. >> Tackle eligible to Jake High or like he was open on that. >> I don't know what happened. Uh I got to look at the film, you know. Um, we got to score in that situation. Uh, whatever it was, we got to find a way to score. So, >> just to clarify, it's it's just more of an upper body injury. Nothing lower body, nothing. >> Yeah, my lower body good. >> Okay, lower body's good. And then there was an um they showed an image of you on the sideline with your um a towel over your head and it looked like you were just really distraught and emotional. Just how hard is it for you at any point in the game to miss just with the history that you have when it comes to injuries? >> Yeah, like I said, I just hinted on it, man. It's just um it's frustrating, you know, but I think the biggest thing is just, you know, I want to be out there, you know, especially in a big moment in a game like that, you know. I'm like I felt I felt like um I just felt like I I needed to be out there, you know. Um obviously we got trust in Tua, you know, whenever he came in, but you know, for me, you know, just how I grew up, how I was raised, like man, it was always, man, fight through it, fight through it, fight through it. And I was trying my best. Um, but I I knew I wasn't where I needed to be to help us win a football game in that in that uh in that moment. So, that's that's how the decision was made. But we'll we'll get back there. >> So, do you think there's like a pressure you're putting on yourself that comes with it? I know you said, "I want to be out there next week and like all the stuff like you just always want to be out there." So, do you think that's like a added pressure internally or anything like that? >> No, it ain't no added pressure. It's just an added drive. You know, I'm I'm going to do whatever I can to make sure I'm back out there. Um, I hated that. I hated I couldn't get back in that game, man. And it's frustrating. But, um, we're going to be good. >> And like a followup, did you kind of talk to, you know, like Kevin and stuff like that about like, hey, I don't think I'm ready to kind of come back in or how was that decision made? Like, who made that decision? >> Yeah. Um, you know, I was I was just trying. I was trying. I was on the sideline. You know, I was sitting there for a while. Like I said, uh, whenever they got the ball first, you know, it just started to get worse and worse. I tried to get up and move around and try to get up and throw see how I felt. Um didn't feel feel the way I wanted to feel and you know that's how the decision was made but I was really talking to the trainers for the most part. They were just making trying to make sure nothing uh was you know emergency wise you know. So >> Mike earlier in the game going back to the connection with Drake London specifically on third down. Walk us through kind of like what you were seeing with him and and uh just uh just especially the third and long conversions with >> um man he's just doing a great job. you know, he obviously he he's one one of our better players on the team. So, uh just whenever we get big time uh situations like that, obviously he's one of the guys we're looking for and uh he made a lot of big time plays on um big time downs for us. So, I mean that's all it was just uh just connecting and you know trusting in our our preparation. >> Mike, it was just kind of a series of unfortunate vates events late down the stretch, your injury included in that. I'm curious how you make sure this moment doesn't kind of derail the juice you guys have had because you have brought an extra punch to this team the last few weeks and games. >> Yeah, we going to be good. Uh it's one game, you know, obviously it's a game that we we felt like we we could have won. We should have won, you know, but like I said, whenever um whenever you got a chance to, you know, you know, close out the game, especially with a good team like that, you got to do it. And uh we didn't do that today. But uh we good. We're in a good spot. Um we're good with where we're at. Obviously, you know, like I just said, you know, the the loss sucks, but you know, we got to be ready for next week. >> Mike, uh, Ravens pass rush was kind of getting in the back field against you, but you were able to elude them a few times, kind of, you know, not running for a ton of yards, but just getting out of the pocket a little bit. How do you feel like you're progressing in in that aspect? >> Yeah, I feel like I'm getting better, stronger every week. So, um, I feel good. I feel real good. So, I'm getting better every week. Anything else? >> This game went differently than the last two games in terms of not relying on the run game as much as as much as you had been. Was that based on looks that they were giving y'all or was that based on sort of the score and the game script and how it played out? >> Yeah, it was looks that they were giving us. Uh they went a couple times just 43, you know, three backers in the game. So, uh, whenever they were getting into that stuff, we were trying to get the ball out, uh, in the air, you know, obviously cuz it's, you know, one less skilled guy on the field, you know, so, um, we felt like that was going to be an advantage and, um, we're just trying to take advantage of the things that things and the looks that they were giving us. So, uh, that's that's why, you know, the game went the way it went this, uh, today. >> Thanks, Mike. >> All right. Thank you. I >> appreciate it. 2.

Jags allowed them to convert four of their first six, but only two of their last nine. And so I think you know the whether it was the coverage, whether the pressure was getting to Jaylen Herz, whatever it was, the Jags defense picked it up in that department as the game went on. >> Yeah. Uh and I do want to take a moment to to to give love to, you know, both uh uh fronts. The the defensive front, I'll start with them. We didn't see a ton of pressure uh uh early on, but they they had pressure when it mattered in in pressure situations. They did well offensively. Again, started slow. Um, and you know, we have some some moments there where we, you know, we're really in it and we kind of let it slip. So there's got to be there's got to be a somewhat of a like I said emphasis on those details. So man, we're going to we're going to learn from this. We're going to have some two really good opportunities to go on the road and just focus on how we can get better ourselves, but more than anything, we want to come back and um with some vengeance whenever, you know, we're here in the dome, we got to play better. Do you find defenses generally know what's coming once you've shown it once or like what is that kind of plug in like that tug and pull process like of you know the guy like you said earlier that anticipated the double move or like had success on the double move earlier but then adjusted to that like does that happen often or is that just something >> um it depends on the situation you know obviously that you know you they get an understanding of the type of routes you can run in certain scenarios that's part of the the chess match of part of the game where you know we're expecting certain coverages too. So he just made a good play on that one. He understood kind of what the scenario was and um we got to be better earlier down where we're not in that long yarded situation trying to go get it. So um just stuff to learn from and we made a good play and I got to we got to be better earlier on. So and that starts with myself. >> When the timing possession is stilted as it was particular in the first and third quarter does that make it difficult to kind of get into a rhythm for the offense? >> Yeah. Um, yeah, we it's tough because we had, you know, early on on three and out when we had put together a good drive, but you only had a couple possessions there. So, it's it's tough whenever you kind of, you know, you're kind of waiting for a while and we got to be better when those details when we get that opportunity. So, and, you know, we can control some of those things for sure and we just got to be be able to play complimentary football as a whole team. I think we're kind of leaving the defense out to dry a couple times and we got to be able to um handle that better. Tyler, what's the I guess level of this team's sense of urgency right now? I mean, it's week five, so it's still early, but you know, you're one and four. I can't imagine you all thought you'd be one and four at this point. >> No, no. I mean, this is not where we envisioned ourselves, where we feel like we're capable of um from a from a unit standpoint. We feel like we got everybody we need in the building and more than anything, it comes from um like you said, a sense of urgency when it comes to our preparation and details. And you know, I think some of our processes have been good. Um, and some of the stuff hasn't bounced our way and we can re-evaluate some of our processes currently in some of those situations um, as far as preparation wise, but I think more than anything, we are ready to go. We understood the mission. You know, they're an undefeated team right now with a really good defense. So, we understand it's going to be it's not going to be easy, but we have to understand that we can control a lot of those mistakes. And I think that's going to be our emphasis going forward is we got to learn how to not lose the game before we win it. We got to, you know, not shoot ourselves in the foot. you keep see saying details like why do you think those aren't consistent like consistently on point? >> Um you know there's there's situations where we can just be a little bit more dialed in and and more than anything it's just it's continued reps continued reps with with all the guys and um it's a new challenge new defense every single week there's different things that may come up and it's how do we kind of um there's going to be mistakes but how do we kind of limit those and not make them drastic in some of those situations. So, I think that's going to be our our our goal going forward. >> I assume you're going to say or you're not going to answer this, but it looked like every time you went down, you were only getting up with like your right hand. Like, was your left hand bothering you out there at all? >> No. No, it wasn't bothering me. It was just kind of a habit probably throughout the week. Um, just not trying to put a bunch of weight on, I guess. But there was no there's no issues throughout the game. Um, didn't really affect me that way. >> Even when >> Even when handing off like to the left, you were using your right. same thing or >> Yeah, just more of a like what I've been doing throughout the week from a rep standpoint, just precaution that way. Um, just made it easier on some of those. So, um, but it continued to get better and better each week. >> Your hand broken the left one. >> Um, there's I'm not even sure if I can answer that, but it was kind of banged up a little bit this week. So, um, didn't really affect me though. Like I said, >> Tyler, when these turnovers happen, I guess what's especially the ones, you know, you caused, what is the mindset you tell yourself to just kind of flush that and get back in the game? >> Um, I I think we do a, you know, did a good job of resetting. We just had some some penalties where now we're behind the eightball and it's tough tough sledding. So, um, like I said, um, I'm I'm guilty of some of those situations where trying to make a play on that interception, just missed it and that's a critical mistake. Can't do that. And then you got some other scenarios where um you know we're driving it, we're driving it, it kind of gets stalled out that way and now we got a punt. So it's it's really tough when you know you're playing that style and and we got everybody we need. It's just kind of how do we just chunk away, chunk away, chunk away and then there's a big one. So again, I'm all stuff to continue to learn from and I'm continuing to learn from that too. You know, there's there's moments where if we're having the right style of of process and play, the good things can happen, but there's some moments where we got to shore up on those little things cuz then the negative stuff kind of um arises. >> The first and second down stuff's come up a few times and so what's the what's the why behind that and how do you address it moving forward? Um there's kind of a balance between trying to be in a good play versus what they're presenting and then also running what we're good at. And that's um the challenge every single week. And it kind of shifts depending on what the flavor of of it is. And um they're obviously I mean they did a really good job. They're, you know, were really well coached, had a good plan. We had a good plan, too, but like I said, there was too many times where we get a penalty or um maybe just a even yardage play or nothing crazy there. and now we're um in a long yardage scenario where that's what they're really good at. So, you know, I think that some of that stuff it's not going to be a perfect drive, but we have to be able to put ourselves flip the field in some of those situations, get ourselves in better scenarios. >> Last week, I think Cam and Chase Young were pretty outspoken after the game. I mean, what was it like today? Do you ever feel as one of the leaders, you know, the call to speak to the team in a in a three-game losing streak like this? I mean, yeah, I think there's an aspect of we got to re-evaluate how we're coming in the building every single day from the the detail standpoint, but there's also a matter of um we're continuing to learn and we're continuing to climb. We took a step in the wrong direction, I would say, today, but it's not a matter of like I said last week, we need to completely flip the script and we need to just change who we are. No. Um it's not that at all. And I'm going to continue to elevate how we prepare as an offense and how we continue to go and that starts with me, too. By no means is there a matter of um we need to cuss people out, do things like that. I mean, we need to continue to do what we're doing from that process and we have the right um we have the right people in the building. We have the right process. It's now let's put it together. Um so, we're going to get that cleaned up and it's going to start with all of us. >> Thank you, sir. Scott Shanley, Kalia Butler joined with Scott. We got to hear from Kellen Moore, Tyler Shuck, Yonas Sanker about whatever which individual person maybe said about this game. >> Well, I think they all kind of said the same thing in different ways. It's about they they understand it's the details of this game that usually result in wins and losses. such a fine line that every team, most teams are are very evenly matched when it comes to talent, evenly matched when it comes to coaching and schematics that everybody spends about the same amount of time throughout the week. But I think as a player and and as a team sometimes when just to get out of that rut, whether it's individually or as a team, you just have to go back to the b the fundamentals throughout the week of practice. And it it starts on how you attack and watch the film. Then it starts in how you take care of your body on the off day on Tuesday. And then just we every day during the week getting finding something to improve on. And I think those are the ways you you bring your confidence back as a player because you you can hear um nobody likes losing. Everybody that spoke, you could hear the disappointment in their voice. But I think it just starts with you don't get to get three games back in in one day. So it starts with just attacking this week on Wednesday, having your best week of practice, and then making the plays in the in the next game in New York when they present themselves. >> Well, something that Yonas Sanker mentioned is now is not a time to start pointing fingers or or getting upset with each other. again the process that you kind of what kind of leadership does that show from a young player on this team but also comparison to last season? He said they had a 1 and 10 start but then they started to figure things out obviously wanting to do that here sooner but what does that look like to you? Yeah, and obviously they they did figure things out late in the end of the year and that that's why there was a lot of um excitement going into this year and a lot of um hope put upon this team, but I think it's exciting because you hear a young player like Sanker, he was thrown into the starting lineup last year. He made plays and now he's already speaking like a season veteran. I think it speaks to the leadership of the coaches developing these young guys into into men early on in their careers, but it also speaks to guys like Cam Jordan and people who have been around here to take those guys under their wing and say if you want to be a pro, this is how you do it. There's a lot of ways to to get out of the league. There's only a handful of ways to stay in the league and I think it's on veteran leadership to show the young guys just how to do it. >> Taking a look ahead at Scott Giants coming up next. This will be an away game. Uh looking at the Giants, they went to overtime with the Commanders today. Jamus Winston threw for over 300 passing yards. Uh what do they present to a Saints team right now? >> Well, they're going to be physical. Coach Harbaugh, obviously anybody who watched him in Baltimore for those years, and now he's with the with the Giants. He's going to have a physical team. He's going to have guys in the line of scrimmage, offensive line, defensive line, who can push people around. So, you're going to have to be ready for a a black and blue type type uh type game. They're going to hand the ball off to Scataboo, but when and when they don't, Thomas has the arm strength. He Jamus likes to air it out. So this team, if you're a DB, just keep the ball in front of you. Make Jamus go the long way cuz he doesn't like to dink and dunk. He's going to take some shots and when he throws it up there, he's just going to make him pay. >> Then they have that Paris game going up against the Steelers who overcame the Colts today 34 to2. Obviously, the big part of that is the fact that they are going to be playing overseas the first game there. But what are the Steelers presenting that could be a good opportunity for the Saints again to rack up some of these wins? Yeah, again the Steelers Hall of Fame quarterback playing. Obviously, they've been playing they've been doing just enough to find a way to win games, but their offense isn't isn't going to break any records. I I I think when you look at this graphic in a hole, these three offenses are not going to be offenses that you're to a points match with where it's back and forth where it turns into a track. get into games like that defensively you have to understand every possession is at a premium because those three teams so it could be battles and in defensive type battles the special teams emerges as well so all three phases >> maybe most importantly coming up after that you're going to have a by week after that how much is that rest maybe needed at this moment especially when you are down a couple >> I'll tell you if they win these three games nobody really wants to go to a buy when you carry that momentum but but the buy comes at at a good time obviously the same team is a little banged up right now, but you get through these three. Hopefully, you you sweep those games, even if you go two and one, you go into that by-week with some confidence and now guys can rest up their body, get their minds rested as well, and then you hit the stretch run for the rest of the season. >> Well, we won't be seeing this team back here for a couple of weeks now, not until the next month going over to New York after this, then Paris. title: Jake Elliott & More on Loss to Jacksonville Jaguars
text: Playing on the on the last kickoff. >> Yeah, I think just we give with the with the time on the clock um the we kind of go over those situations all the time um what we want to do there. We decided to keep it in there and and try to make a tackle and um hindsight's 20/20 but it didn't didn't work this time. >> Given how quick the the turnaround was after you made your kick, is there enough time [clears throat] to talk it over or is it just like you get you get the >> I mean yeah, I got to get the I get relayed the info of what the plan is and go out there and try to execute. >> I'm sure those are situations you guys talk through why with that much time would would that be this that decision? >> That's that's got to be a a question for coach I think. He's got stipulations on certain amount I don't know exactly what the amount of time is but um didn't work this time. >> Since you guys run through those things, were you surprised by the decision or is what is it what you expected to >> Honestly, kind of like you said there was so little time for me to kind of gather myself between those two things. I I just went out and did what what I was told and um you know, I wish it obviously turned out better. >> Were you hoping were you hoping that last kick would have ended the game? >> Yeah, I mean I always think you want to end the game with a kick there and not have to go back out for try to cover a kick but um it's not how it played out unfortunately and um go back and and look at it and learn from it and see maybe if it if that changes going forward but um yeah. >> What about this I guess 2 minutes like from the the highs to the lows and you >> Yeah, it sucks. I mean you come all this way um you know, you think you're in the driver's seat to win a big game and um and now now now we're feeling feeling pretty down. >> Kind of crazy what happened on the opening kickoff. What did you see there? >> Um just I didn't see a whole lot. Kind of just opened up on me quick and then um uh I don't I don't know exactly what happened. I know Troy got held and kind of led to a big scuffle there but um >> He He was the player that actually drew the penalty >> Yeah, I believe so. I believe so looking back at it but after all it's so hard for me to see all that stuff. >> And on the last one are you able to see if they did anything different on their return? >> I can't I can't really tell um what's going on up front there. I'm just kind of tracking the ball after I hit it and trying to get into a safety position. >> On the go-ahead field goal, how'd you feel? >> Uh I felt good. It was I was I was excited about it, obviously. Um had a lot of confidence that we were going to get that drive accomplished and get back into range. And um so So, obviously felt really good in the moment. And um you know, I wish that was, like I said, the last one. >> Have you ever had that big a swing of emotions? >> I don't know, man. I don't know. Uh probably not not in that way, anyway. >> What was Nick's message to the team after the game? The last I guess. >> Um I mean, just hell of a battle, obviously. Um go back and look at you know, some of the situational stuff and what we can improve on there. >> Was that a group discussion between Michael and Nick? >> I believe so. I mean, I don't I don't know how the how it works in the headsets there. I'm just kind of relaying the info and I'm doing what I'm told. >> As one of the special teams leaders, what message did you convey to the team? >> Yeah, I mean, we were First of all, hell of a fight with all the guys that went down. We were kind of piecing piecing things together there. Guys were playing in positions that they never played before or you know, Clay was coaching guys up on the sideline that have never played punt. And um so total total team effort there. Um with a lot of bodies that that haven't been out there. So, um proud of Cole for him stepping in. I mean, he hasn't really done that before. So, um there's there's a lot of guys that that came in and contributed. So, I'm I'm proud of that fight. Obviously, we're we're inexperienced a little bit in those spots right now. So, so a lot of learning. >> How much did it hurt to lose Trot? >> Yeah, I mean, Trot, every side of the ball he plays, he he brings so much energy and um you know, he's he's obviously one of our big leaders on on special teams. So, uh we missed him missed him a lot. >> I know it's it's and hitting an hitting an explosive. It's one of those things, but I wish I was able to look up at the clock for another another second, you know, run off before it happened. It's one of those things. >> I was just going to ask you, you had no idea, right? >> No. No, he's in that moment just trying to try to get a guy down. >> Do you know Do you know what the issues were in terms of that seam being open? >> Uh no, I mean I think they just was able to exploit something. You know, we've been doing covering kicks pretty good all night. Um I think they found something they liked and they were able to hit it and kind of opened up there. >> Was there any discussion of kicking it deep? Do you think Did you hear anything about that? >> Uh no, cuz I mean I'm taking typically not on kickoff. We had some guys go down and then I kind of jumped in at the last second, you know, but you know, whatever decisions are made, you know, we got to stick by them, but most important thing, we just got to execute, you know, whether you kick it in, kick it out, you know, you still got to execute. >> Typically when you're on that unit, do you know like what the plan is in terms of whether you're going to try to what kind of kick it's going to be? >> Yeah, I mean I knew we were kicking it in bounds. Um you know, try to force them to you know, return the ball, run some time off the clock. Um you just got to go out there and execute. >> How gut-wrenching was this loss though overall? >> That was a tough one. Uh we work hard during the week. Um you know, we work really hard, you know, everyone does, but um just to have it, you know, lose a game like that that way is always tough. >> When you made that tackle, did you think that it was over? >> I did. I looked up on the clock, saw zero start, it was over. Um then 1 second got put back on, so it's tough. >> Did they do anything differently on that kick return to kind of set up the long run? >> Uh some of that we have to go back and look, trying to see what exactly they did to execute, but like I said, they found a seam and you know, made a play. >> Give us an idea of the range of emotions when there's such a swing at the end with two kicks like that. >> Yeah, I mean it's going to take us a minute to process this one. I don't know if I've been a part of a game this kind of just like gut-wrenching in a minute, you know what I mean? So it's uh it's going to take us a day to to get over this one, you know, and we have to and we will, you know, we have a good We've got a good group of guys and coaches that help you move on, but man, it it really was just a gut-wrenching loss, you know what I mean? So. >> Obviously, you had some really good returns. Special teams was playing well. Just how difficult is it to end the game like that after after a made kick by Jake? >> Yeah, I mean, people go into fight or flight mode. It's it's like when you got game point in ping pong or tennis, right? And and someone's just there surviving and and uh you know, we can look back and say we should have done this, we should have done this. At the end of the day, at the end of the day, we didn't and it sucks, but you have to pick yourself off the off the mat and I know people are going to be furious and you know, just don't doubt for 1 second that everyone in this locker room is not furious. You know, we're taking this lightly. So, there's things we got to get fixed. Um but uh but I really do love love this group, you know, love this group of receivers that I'm with and and uh something we're going to talk about, you know, is linking arms, standing together through it. So, you find out who you really are in adversity, not when things are going well. >> What was Nick's main message to you guys after a loss like this? >> Uh just that we have to own it. He'll Nick is so great at owning things, you know. Um and we try and follow his lead, you know, and we'll own it and you know, that's what I say. People are going to be mad and don't question for a second if people in this room are mad because we're all frustrated, furious, going to do everything we can to fix it. Um but Nick is wonderful at owning things and we all try to follow his lead. >> Appreciate your time. >> Thank you. >> I told the guys earlier in this week and and last night that I don't I don't care what injuries we have, what the offense does, what situation we're in. Um we play the situation we're put in and it it it doesn't matter because if the Jags don't score any points, they don't win. So, um it doesn't matter what what situation we're put in. We just got to attack it and and get after it. >> I'm sorry if you've been asked this, but can you kind of describe what you know, how you made that stop on fourth down >> Mhm. Yeah, there were a lot of timeouts in between, so we got to look at a couple of different pictures to get a gist of what they you know, looking in the back Damien in there. >> No, man. He I think he left that up to me, you know. I mean, he he would say some [snorts] encouraging things to them, but again, you know, we all have a role to play and we all have our 1/11 and you know, Jay did his part, you know, and I have to do my part as a leader. I lead by example and uh he left that to me this week. >> And how did you handle all that? >> That's just the theme of just again, like, you know, you see me doing this, you see me doing this. Ride the wave. Again, wave of good, wave of bad, doesn't matter what it looks like. Just keep keep surfing. And then keep going and um you know, finish. That was that was the uh the theme as well. So, those two themes right there. >> Yeah, you probably never had a week like this before >> No. >> kind of like >> Dude, I'm tired. I'm so tired. >> [snorts] >> So tired. John, welcome. >> Your your head coach, Nick Sirianni, just told everybody that he takes responsibility for the loss and he told you that he cost you guys the game. What is it like when you're when your when your head coach is accountable with the public and and telling you guys that after the game? >> [sighs] >> I mean, it's not just on Sirianni, it's on us as well, you know. I I can't be false starting on, you know, certain got to have a periods when we're backed up and, you know, we're not extending drives cuz of that and it's it's not just on coach. Although coach can say that in the media, I think we're all looking at what we can improve on as a team and as individuals because we all have a play today contributed in the loss. It's not just Nick's fault. We all have plays. >> Is there such a thing as a moral victory for you? >> I don't even know what that means now. I don't even know. Like, my brain hurts. This week has been a week from hell for me. Yeah, [snorts] and then I don't even know the concept of a moral victory right now. I just again, trying to look internally to see how I contributed to this loss so I can correct it because we weren't good enough. We know that. Um you know, certain downs and certain plays during the second half, you know, we got to be better executing. Um but I will say I was very proud of of my line up front. Um you know, the theme this week um and during the game was just to keep riding the wave, wave of good, wave of bad, wave of uh perfect, wave of adversity, and just keep surfing. And what that means is just to keep playing the next play. Um and I thought they did a great job of that. They listened. Um and then ultimately, you know, with Jay's confidence and Jay's poise, put us in the position to make plays in the game to win this game. And unfortunately, they made plays to win the game. >> Coach, last week you talked about how like, you know, you can't have guys keep the locker pointing fingers. That kind of that usually breaks teams apart. Um obviously, it seemed like that [clears throat] was the case this past week despite everything last week. >> I'm I feel about this Yeah, [clears throat] I'm I'm actually very very um excited and very high on the team right now because I think more than ever, you know, defense picked us up. Not just on the field, but you know, with everything we went through this week, they picked us up and off the field. And we did link arms. And I think we have a forward. Yeah, we're linking arms even even more now. There's no blame to be be tossed around. And again, it's how can I do my 1/11th and how can I contribute to a win? Unfortunately, we lost. So, now it's how did my 1/11th contribute to the loss? And that's how we have to look at it. And so, you know, again, there were moments in the game that we all want back and we all contributed, but yeah, it's tough. >> You mentioned emotional hell during the what is weighing heavily on you? >> I mean, Mike, what do you think? Everything. I mean, it's just everything. You know, we got one of the greatest tackles ever played this game retire. Trades, you know, you got to deal with everything. You know, as it comes to my best friends. You know, not the same team anymore that Yeah, I've got to do a better job of Not even a better job. I just got to just be better, you know. But, it's I think it's self-explanatory, to be honest. I don't need to explain that. >> From an emotional standpoint, how do you get over a week like the one you just had? >> Uh watch the film and move on. >> I don't [cough] understand the game. [clears throat] I mean >> Yeah, no, you just I mean, just watch the film. >> Um Nick Sirianni just now said he made the wrong decision on on that last kickoff and he cost the team the game. What's What's your reaction when your head coach comes out and says that about kicking off uh to the Jaguars? >> We're going to stand by our coach no matter what it is through thick and thin. Um we're wrong. And that's the best mentality you can have. Of course, when situations like this happen, it's um it's easy for um teams to kind of separate with their connection and things like that. So, uh and it's evident when we go through adversity, we stick together and we stay together no matter what it is, no matter um who um it may fall on, no matter what um what the situation may be or adversity we go through. So, and just continue to lock arms and just stay together and should continue to move forward. >> Obviously, they kicked off. They're returning. How deflating is it when somebody can't make that tackle, you know, on the other side of the field? >> Um they made they get paid, too. Uh um so, their coaches um as well as their players. So, they made a good blocking scheme and they made and they made a good play, simple as that. We have to go out there and just execute and um be physical and get our blocks and get the guy down. >> Have you ever been a part of emotions like that where Jake makes a field goal like that and then it goes the other way with I mean, their their backup long snapper defensive tackles making the, you know, snapping the ball? >> Um it's the name of the game, man. Um next man up. It's a huge game of emotions. all right. always got to try to stay even-keeled, you know, cuz anything can happen, as I said before. Um other [clears throat] guys get paid, too, you know, to make big plays just as we do, you know, so um in that situation, we just got to continue to stay stay together and just continue to work and just stay even keel as you go through all the ups and downs of the game. >> Appreciate you. >> Yes, sir. And I'll give us an idea being out there on special teams in that moment when when the kickoff is being run back, um what the plan was and then just how deflating is it all? >> I feel like every time we lined up, the plan is always to go down and then make the play. Feel like unfortunately in this position, we wasn't able to do so, so and I mean, we was just forced to look back and watch him return it and eventually they kicked the field goal. I mean, definitely suck to be in that position. Something that we got to uh go back, watch film, learn from it, so it doesn't happen again. >> Have you ever really been in a range of emotions like that at the end of a game where a kick is made by Jake and then it goes the other way and they have a have a backup long snapper come in, a defensive tackle, part of the operation? >> Uh I wouldn't say I have. Definitely suck to be in that position. I mean, it suck. I mean, just given the fact that we made the field goal prior and being that position at the end of the game, uh never want to be in that position again, for sure. >> What was the uh the main message from coaches and Nick Sirianni after after losing such, you know, you guys played well enough, especially defensively, to win, um but losing a game like that last second. >> Uh we got to stay together. That's what it comes down to. I mean, at the end of the day, we're a team. Uh we got to stay together, find a way to come back next week and get a win. >> Nick Sirianni just now with the media said uh he made a mistake at the end of the game and cost the team the game. And I guess he says he told that to you guys in the locker room. What what is it like when you have a head coach come in here after a loss like that and be accountable for his >> Yeah, it's very um make you know, makes us as players feel good. Um you know, just taking accountability.
